name: take_screenshot
description: Take a screenshot of one display right now and return it as an image. IMPORTANT: without display_id it captures the display currently under the mouse cursor (which moves between calls) — pass display_id from list_displays whenever you care which monitor you get. Set full_resolution=true only when you need to read small text. To capture one window (even if covered by others), use capture_window instead.

display_id.description: Display id from list_displays (optional; default = display under the mouse cursor)

full_resolution.description: Return native resolution instead of the downscaled version

name: take_screenshot_region
description: Screenshot a rectangle of the screen. Coordinates are GLOBAL virtual-desktop DIP — exactly the space list_displays bounds use, so any monitor (including negative origins) works directly. A region spanning several monitors is clipped to the one holding its largest part (the reply says what was actually captured).

x.description: Global virtual-desktop X (DIP, may be negative)

y.description: Global virtual-desktop Y (DIP, may be negative)

display_id.description: Optional: force this display (coordinates stay global)

name: list_windows
description: List the user's open top-level windows: id, title, app, bounds (global DIP), display_id, minimized. Use the id or title with capture_window. On macOS only id and title are available (bounds/display_id are null).

name: capture_window
description: Capture ONE window's own surface by id (from list_windows) or title substring. Works even when the window is covered by other windows, off-screen or on any monitor — unlike take_screenshot, which grabs the visible framebuffer. Minimized windows cannot be captured (ask the user to restore them). Window ids are ephemeral (the OS recycles them): take them from a FRESH list_windows call, and pass title together with window_id as a staleness guard.

window_id.description: Window id from list_windows (preferred — unambiguous; a number on Windows, a string on macOS)

title.description: Case-insensitive window title substring (used when window_id is absent)

full_resolution.description: Return native resolution instead of the downscaled version

name: ask_user_to_select_region
description: Open the interactive selection overlay so the USER can mark the exact area to show you. Use when you need the user to point at something. Waits up to 2 minutes.

name: get_last_screenshot
description: Return the most recent screenshot the user took with Shotik.

name: list_screenshots
description: List recent screenshots from Shotik history (paths, sizes, timestamps). Recordings: list_recordings.

name: list_recordings
description: List recent recordings made with Shotik, newest first: audio (calls, voice notes; .m4a) and screen video. Returns file paths with kind, duration and size, so you can transcribe or analyze them. Shotik itself does not transcribe; for speech-to-text extract mono 16 kHz audio, e.g. `ffmpeg -i <file> -ac 1 -ar 16000 out.wav`.

kind.description: Only audio recordings or only screen videos

name: get_last_recording
description: Return the most recent Shotik recording (file path, kind, duration, size, time). Use kind "audio" for the last recorded call. The file is not inlined — read or transcribe it from the path.

kind.description: Only the last audio recording or only the last screen video

name: list_displays
description: List the user's displays: id, bounds (DIP coordinates), scale factor, primary flag.
